key_insight: Established RCT methods are still useful for measuring AI-driven human uplift, but frontier AI systems systematically violate key RCT assumptions (e.g., non‑stationarity, interference, scale, adaptivity). The paper maps those failure modes and offers concrete design, analysis, and governance fixes so RCTs yield reliable, high‑stakes evidence.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap between traditional RCT practice and the distinctive properties of frontier AI systems that can bias or invalidate human uplift studies, preventing misleading conclusions in deployment and governance decisions.
method: Systematically diagnose how frontier-AI properties (non‑stationarity, emergent behavior, interference/contagion, heterogeneity, scale) conflict with core RCT assumptions.

Propose practical adjustments for study design and analysis (e.g., pre-registration, stratification and blocking, interference-aware designs, sequential monitoring, robust estimands, simulation-based power checks) plus operational safety/privacy controls.
Provide actionable guidance: checklists, templates, and governance processes to link study results to high‑stakes deployment decisions safely.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners and evaluators concise, implementable methods to run and interpret human uplift RCTs for frontier systems, reducing the risk of erroneous policy or deployment decisions and improving evidence quality.
visual_elements: Side‑by‑side diagram: standard RCT assumptions vs frontier AI violations (icons for non‑stationarity, interference, scale).
Study lifecycle flowchart: design → safety & privacy checks → run (with sequential monitoring) → analysis (robust estimands) → governance/decision node.
Risk‑mitigation matrix: common failure modes (rows) × recommended fixes (columns).
Example visualization: sequential monitoring/power curve or stratified effect heatmap showing heterogeneous uplift.
paper_title: RCTs & Human Uplift Studies: Methodological Challenges and Practical Solutions for Frontier AI Evaluation
paper_authors: Patricia Paskov, Kevin Wei, Shen Zhou Hong, Dan Bateyko, Xavier Roberts-Gaal
